regions.merged_text: We made some calls next day after Holy Mass and Breakfast -- Fr. M. J. and I serving each other in turn at the Convent -- and about 2 P.M. left via Sault Ste. Marie to reach Superior about 5:30 -6 o'clock. To our pleasant surprise, whom did we meet at the depot but our old friend Ed Sampson, and his wife, waiting to convey us to the Parish House on 12th and John Sts. She had phoned me a day or two before I left Detroit that they were starting off on their vacation and possibly would see us in Superior. The celebration next day, Feast of the Assumption, was a happy one. Fr. M. Joachim and I having offered our Holy Masses earlier, were ready as deacon and sub-deacon, to assist Fr. Edward at the Solemnity proper. The Rt. Rev. Bishop Reverman attended in state, and Fr. Weber (now Rt. Rev. Msgr.) gave the sermon. The latter is now Vicar General and looks very well. Thanks be to God, everything went off smoothly, both at the Jubilee Mass itself, and at the receptions. The first of these took place immediately after the solemnity in church, when quite a procession of friends came to the school-hall to greet the Celebrant and his Reverend Brothers. The other con- sisted of a gathering of about fifty or more friends for dinner, and a program in a hotel down on Tower Ave. Besides a goodly number of Fr. Edward's class-mates from Sacred Heart School, a number of our cousins and other relatives and old friends from Burkhardt, Detroit, etc. attended. We made quite a number of visits -- taking altogether -- that evening, next day and Tuesday. These visits, though not exactly canonical had more or less the nature of missionary work. Monday A. M. Fr. Joachim and I served each other's Masses in St. Joseph's Convent, down near the East end. What a change in 50 years! They wondered when I told them that I used to carry them on the trolley-cars as they went daily back and forth to school -- only two or three in the whole community. Now they must number about thirty in that Convent, as seemed to me. One of them present remembered those pioneer days. To another, now an invalid seemingly just waiting to take off for Heaven I had the privilege of giving Holy Communion. Deo Gratias. That P. M. we went to bless a little ten year old grand- daughter of Teacher Aggie Murphy Oteir in the "Steel Plant", and some others. I was surprised at the seemingly little change in her appearance in twenty-six years, when she attended Fr. M. Joachim's first Holy Mass.
